attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel renders full_name and postal_code for every confirmed signer. This directly violates the agreed rule that public signer lists show at most first name, last initial and city, and it discloses personal data of EU and US signers to any visitor. The release text itself says the panel shows first name + last initial, so the template contradicts the stated behavior. QA marked this panel as Pass without checking it against the privacy rule.

The newsletter opt-in checkbox is pre-checked and bundled into the sign action. GDPR requires consent to be affirmative, unambiguous and freely given, so EU signers would be opted into organizer marketing by default. The organizer CSV export is built on this invalid consent.

GDPR is stated to apply, but the artifact gives no privacy notice, lawful basis, retention period for confirmed signatures' email and postal code, or handling of access and erasure requests. Only unconfirmed signatures have a purge rule.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: GDPR notice/lawful basis, retention policy for confirmed signer data, and data-subject rights (erasure/withdrawal) handling

attacks.claim: The error flow does not meet the agreed WCAG 2.1 AA requirement. The form uses novalidate, and invalid fields are marked only by border and background colour. sign.js never writes text into the aria-live .form-error region. Inputs have no aria-invalid or aria-describedby linkage. Screen-reader users get no error identification or suggestion (1.4.1, 3.3.1, 3.3.3).
attacks.evidence: for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); ...

attacks.claim: The only accessibility evidence is an automated axe scan of the sign page. It cannot detect the missing error-message and state-association problems, and it does not cover the error states, the recent-signers panel or the live-count updates. It does not establish WCAG 2.1 AA conformance for the public flow.
attacks.evidence: | axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations |

attacks.claim: Client submit handling is incomplete. Only 422 and ok are handled, so 409 (duplicate), 429 and 500 responses and network failures give the user no feedback. The 422 path also assumes every returned field name exists in form.elements, and an empty or unexpected fields array throws. With novalidate, all validation depends on this path.

The rollback plan only swaps the UI back to a Follow button. It does not address signatures and personal data already collected, pending unconfirmed rows, queued confirmation emails, the purge job, or opt-in records. Beyond the two error-rate metrics, it names no go/no-go action thresholds, alerting or owner for the 24h watch.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip `petitions_signing` off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button.

attacks.claim: Data residency depends on postal codes resolving to an EU country, but the artifact gives no rule for ambiguous or unresolvable codes. EU signers' personal data could land in us-east-1.
attacks.evidence: eu-central-1 for EU-resolved postal codes, us-east-1 otherwise

attacks.claim: No CSRF protection or per-IP/per-email rate limiting is described for the public sign endpoint. The endpoint could be used for mass fake signatures or to email-bomb arbitrary addresses with confirmation emails.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: CSRF token and per-IP/per-email rate limit on POST /p/{slug}/sign

attacks.claim: The submit button has no disabled or loading state during the fetch, which invites double submissions. The recent-signers list has no empty state.
attacks.evidence: const res = await fetch(form.action, { method: 'POST', body: new FormData(form) }); ABSENT: submit disabled/loading state
